raw_answer_text:
A1: Every station on the segment — the request is sent as a broadcast (dst MAC ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff), reaching all hosts, not just B.
A2: The host lacks the MAC address mapping for B's IP (node A is described as "wants MAC for B's IP"), so it has no cached entry to use.
A3: NOT STATED.
A4: No — the file states other hosts on the LAN simply hear the broadcast and it is "heard, ignored," with no reply edge shown from them.
A5: It is sent directly to just the requesting host (unicast, dst MAC = A's MAC).
A6: It caches the IP→MAC binding, resulting in an entry mapping B's IP to aa:bb:cc:... in A's ARP cache (shown in the table as "after segment 2").
A7: The requesting host does not know the target's hardware address — obtaining it is precisely the purpose of the "who-has B?" request.
A8: NOT STATED.
